question: A framework agreement for trade and economic cooperation between the EU and Argentina setting out specific cooperation agreements on fisheries, the use of nuclear energy and scientific and technological cooperation has been in force since 1990. However, the President of Argentina, Javier Milei, intends to arbitrarily cancel, under the ‘Omnibus Law’, the fishing rights of almost eighty fishing vessels and companies backed by Galician funds. 1.

In light of the above, can the European Commission, specifically its High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy and Vice-President, ensure that the EU delegation looks into this threat to European companies established in Argentina and analyse the possible and far-reaching consequences of this decision by the Argentine President on the economy and food supply, since these companies supply fish and aquaculture products to the European market?
Furthermore, what is the status of the aforementioned framework cooperation agreement?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.4.2024) The Framework Agreement for trade and economic cooperation between the European Economic Community and the Argentine Republic1 was signed in 1990 and remains in force. The Agreement has been the legal basis for developing a large number of dialogues and cooperation initiatives between the EU and Argentina for more than 30 years.
It was complemented between 1994 and 1999 by an additional agreement on fisheries2, which was not renewed when its initial period of validity ended in 1999.

The EU Delegation in Argentina is in constant contact with Member States’ trade counsellors and EU businesses based or operating in Argentina, in particular through its close relation with the Eurocámara that brings together the bi-national chambers of commerce of Member States. The EU Delegation also monitors legislative and economic developments that may affect EU interests, including those of EU companies.

According to the latest information available, the Commission can inform the Honourable Member that, on 31 January 2024, the government of President Javier Milei withdrew the articles affecting the fishing industry from the so-called ‘Omnibus law’ that the President sent to the Argentine Congress on 27 December 2023 modifying a large number of elements of Argentina’s economic regulations.

Therefore, the rights of the mixed capital companies involved in fishing activities (often from Argentina and Spain) referred to in the Honourable Member’s question are unaffected. The EU Delegation in Argentina will continue to monitor the situation closely.
1 Framework Agreement for trade and economic cooperation between the European Economic Community and

the Argentine Republic - Exchange of Letters, OJ L 295, 26.10.1990, p. 67–73. 2 Agreement on relations in the sea fisheries sector between the European Economic Community and the Argentine Republic - Exchange of Letters - Protocol I establishing the fishing opportunities and financial compensation provided for in the Agreement on relations in the sea fisheries sector between the Argentine Republic and the European Economic Community, OJ L 318, 20.12.1993 pp. 0002 – 0017.
